title: Fixed-geometry size shuffles raised mean modeled failure variance in two selected mouse contact sets
abstract: We tested contact size assignment at fixed geometry in 1,519 selected Allen V1 Deep Dive connections and 1,472 MICrONS connections. Each connection kept both cell identities, all positions and its full size list. In a Poisson ball failure model with radius 10 micrometres and contact survival probability 0.9, observed mean variance ratios were 1.311695 and 1.255645. Exact within-connection size-shuffle means were 1.324622 and 1.264990. The observed values were 0.98% and 0.74% lower. Tests with 4,999 draws gave two-map corrected probabilities of 0.0008 and 0.0112. Scalar and exhaustive checks agreed within 9e-16. This is a new conditional test on existing panels, not new animals. One animal per panel, uncalibrated size weights, assumed failures and possible spatial gradients prevent a physiological reliability or optimization claim. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. Input records stay outside the publication.

display.caption: Observed size placement and fixed-geometry size shuffles under an assumed local-failure model. Bars show conditional null ranges, not uncertainty across animals.
